summary: Verified the direct Turso HTTP pipeline, populated record count, Worker UI/query implementation, and Wrangler bindings. Turso returned exactly 271 link records and sample records contained required fields.

critical.issue: Turso auth token is hardcoded in both source and Wrangler [vars], exposing a database write credential in repository/deployment configuration. Move it to a Wrangler secret and remove the fallback token from source.

action_items: Rotate the exposed Turso token, store it with wrangler secret put TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN, and remove hardcoded token fallbacks.
Run a deployed Worker smoke test for /api/links and /api/stats after deployment; only the Turso endpoint and source configuration were tested here.
critical_code_review_comments: Do not commit database bearer tokens in cloudflare-worker.js or wrangler.toml [vars]; this grants write access and can be extracted by anyone with repository/deployment access.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Direct Turso pipeline https://shindora-player-shindora-stream.aws-ap-northeast-1.turso.io/v2/pipeline responded successfully; COUNT(*) links is 271. Worker source has queryTurso, embedded dashboard/player UI, and Wrangler URL/token bindings. Deployed Worker URL was not provided/tested.
rca of the issue: The implementation includes TURSO_DEFAULT_TOKEN in JavaScript and TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN under Wrangler [vars], so the credential is shipped as plaintext rather than injected as a secret. Functionality passes, but credential exposure is a deployment-security defect.
